summary: Unexpected overage alert and invoice spike after model-variant rollback
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart received automated overage alerts for their dedicated account after a model-variant rollback performed during a canary deploy window. The account shows a ~42% spike in token usage between 2026-03-09T22:00Z and 2026-03-10T02:00Z, which does not match BrightCart's traffic patterns or application logs.

Impact:
- Customer received an immediate overage email, triggering an emergency billing review request.
- BrightCart disabled nonessential traffic to the inference endpoints to avoid further charges.
- Potential invoice adjustment and credit needed if metering error is confirmed.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dpool-us-east-3
- Region: us-east-1
- Customer org: org-BR-0012 (BrightCart)
- Time window: 2026-03-09 22:00 to 2026-03-10 02:00 UTC

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Customer continued normal traffic to their chat endpoint during our canary rollout.
2) We rolled the model variant back at ~2026-03-09T23:45Z after elevated latency was observed in the canary.
3) Customer saw immediate token accounting spike and received overage alert.

Observed behavior:
- Metering export shows duplicated token entries for ~18k requests during the window.
- Each duplicated entry accounts for full-response token count, effectively doubling recorded tokens for affected requests.

Expected behavior:
- Metering should be idempotent for retries and rollbacks. Rollbacks/route changes should not create duplicated billing records for the same request_id.

Logs / Evidence attached:
- Billing export CSV: s3://billing-exports/prod/2026-03-09/brightcart_tokens.csv (internal link)
- Metering job run: metering-job-20260310-03 (logs: https://logs.redwood.internal/metering/2026-03-10/03)
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 04:30: Diego R. - Initial look: Found repeated request_id values in metering table but two separate ingresses recorded the same request after rollback.

2026-03-10 06:15: SRE team - Ingress A (api-gw-1) retried requests to Ingress B (api-gw-2) when routing mesh paths changed; retries were logged with new trace ids but preserved original request_id header in ~60% of cases.

2026-03-10 07:00: Billing - Metering pipeline currently dedupes on (request_id, timestamp) but does not consider retries across different route_ids; dedupe window is 30s which allowed duplicates when rollback caused delayed retries.

2026-03-10 09:20: Engineering hypothesis: Rollback triggered upstream proxy retries + our router created transient duplicate deliveries; metering consumed both deliveries as separate events because dedupe key omitted 'routing_event_id'.
2026-03-10 11:00: Reproduced in staging by forcing routing-change during active requests: saw duplicated metering records when request was replayed due to a 503-to-200 retry path.
workaround: Temporary workaround implemented 2026-03-10 12:20: Turned on immediate throttling on BrightCart's dedicated pool to limit additional duplicate attempts and suppressed overage email notifications while we investigate.
resolution: Pending. Short-term customer relief: Billing agrees to provisional credit for the duplicated token volume (approx. 42% of the spike) conditional on final validation. Engineering patch scheduled: Update metering dedupe key to include routing_event_id and extend dedupe window during rollouts; rollout PR targeting 2026-03-14 (INT-4120). Follow-up actions: full replay of metering pipeline for the affected time window to compute final adjustment, and apply credit or invoice correction to BrightCart if duplicates confirmed.

2026-03-10 12:40 - SRE (L. Chen): 'Applied temporary routing guard to prevent cross-ingress retries during rollouts. This suppressed duplicate deliveries for live traffic.'

2026-03-13 16:10 - Diego Ramirez (Engineering): 'Patch merged to include routing_event_id in dedupe key: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4521. Staging tests look good. Production rollout scheduled for 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC.'
